Apple has waited a very long time to launch its first foldable iPhone, while Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold series has already evolved to its eighth generation.

Apple always had good reasons to wait, but Samsung's latest experience suggests the iPhone maker's timing could hardly be better...

Apple's Long Wait

Samsung was among the earliest companies to push foldable smartphones hard, but quickly found that the Korean giant had moved too fast. The first-generation Samsung Galaxy Fold had an extremely fragile display, forcing Samsung to recall it from the market.

Meanwhile, Apple has patiently waited for display technology to mature—to the point where it is not only clearly more durable, but also shows no obvious crease when opened. Reports say Apple had to send its own design engineers to help Samsung achieve this goal.

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Shows the Time Is Right

We mentioned last month that the display on Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 is very likely to be extremely similar to the one prepared for the iPhone Ultra. Our sister site 9to5Google found that it absolutely delivers on that promise, with the crease in the middle of the screen nearly invisible when opened.

But it's not just that Samsung has finally got the display technology right—consumer demand also appears to have finally arrived. 9to5Google reports that initial demand for the Fold 8 is three times that of its predecessor.

This figure is also built on top of last year's fifty percent growth in demand.

Of course, the two are likely related—a crease-free display greatly boosts appeal—but factoring in last year's growth, it seems foldable phones have been around long enough for more people to see the benefits of this type of device.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to launch next month alongside the iPhone 18 Pro series. Expectations are that this device will quickly capture around 25% of the entire foldable smartphone market.
